content: 1. Discontinue or reduce the dosage of pitolisant by half as necessary. 2. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Polatuzumab vedotin undergoes catabolism into small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a substrate of CYP3A4. Co-administration of polatuzumab vedotin with strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease the area under the curve (AUC) of unconjugated MMAE. 4. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 5. Prednisone decreases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, etravirine reduces the levels or effects of prednisone through the same mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 6. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of primaquine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 7. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic enzymes CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 8. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel, micronized progesterone, and natural progesterone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 9. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of quetiapine and quinidine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 10. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 11. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of repaglinide and ribociclib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Ribociclib, in turn, increases the levels or effects of etravirine through the same mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 12. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 13. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 14. Etravirine increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 15. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of riociguat by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely, as dose adjustment data is unavailable. 16. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 17. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 18. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of sildenafil by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Potent CYP3A4 inducers are expected to significantly decrease sildenafil plasma levels. 19. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of solifenacin and sorafenib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 20. Sparsentan reduces the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 21. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C19 substrates if adverse reactions occur during co-administration with stiripentol. 22. Etravirine decreases the effects of sufentanil SL by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may reduce sufentanil levels and efficacy, potentially causing withdrawal syndrome in physically dependent patients. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations. 23. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 24. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of sunitinib and suvorexant by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease suvorexant efficacy; if dose adjustment is required, do not exceed 20 mg/day. 25. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of tacrolimus and tadalafil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 26. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of tamoxifen by influencing hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibition decreases tamoxifen metabolism to N-desmethyl tamoxifen, an active metabolite with similar biological activity. 27. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of tamsulosin and tasimelteon by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration of tasimelteon with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 28. Tazemetostat reduces the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 29. Tecovirimat increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19 and a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness during co-administration. 30. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of temsirolimus, teniposide, and terbinafine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 31. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of tetracycline and theophylline by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 32. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of tiagabine and ticagrelor by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Avoid using ticagrelor with potent CYP3A4 inducers. 33. Ticlopidine increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of ticlopidine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 34. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole and tofacitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Loss of or decreased response to tofacitinib may occur when co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inducers. 35. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of tolterodine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 36. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 37. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of toremifene by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inducers increase the rate of toremifene metabolism, lowering its steady-state serum concentration. 38. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of tramadol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 39. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 40. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of triazolam by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 41. Triclabendazole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. If plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates are elevated during triclabendazole use, recheck plasma concentrations after discontinuation of triclabendazole. 42. Ublituximab decreases the effects of etravirine through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of valbenazine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 44. Valproic acid increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 45. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of vardenafil and vemurafenib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 46. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of verapamil through the same mechanism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 47. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of vilazodone by increasing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider increasing the vilazodone dose up to twofold (not exceeding 80 mg/day) when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers for more than 14 days. 48. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of voriconazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 49. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of vortioxetine by increasing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 50. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 51. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of warfarin by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. It also decreases the levels or effects of warfarin through other mechanisms. Monitor INR more frequently if co-administered with inducers of these isoenzymes and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 52. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 53. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 54. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of alfentanil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 55. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. It also decreases the levels or effects of alosetron by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 56. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of amitriptyline and amlodipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 57. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 58. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of armodafinil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 59. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of atazanavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. However, packaging labeling states that etravirine and atazanavir/ritonavir can be co-administered without dose adjustments, as the decrease in atazanavir is not clinically relevant when all three drugs are used. 60. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of bosentan by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. It also decreases the levels or effects of bosentan by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown.
